newsitem.title: USA: US home mortgage rates fall in week.
newsitem.headline: US home mortgage rates fall in week.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages fell 10 basis points to an average 8.06 percent in the week ended October 4 from 8.16 percent the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
Fifteen-year mortgages also fell the same number of basis points to an average 7.58 percent from 7.68 percent the prior week, Freddie Mac said.
One-year adjustable-rate mortgages dropped 12 basis points to an average 5.70 percent from 5.82 percent in the week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.57 percent, the 15-year 7.09 percent, and the ARM 5.76 percent.

"The Federal Reserve's decision last week not to raise interest rates reduced inflation fears of many investors, helping interest rates fall this week," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said.
"Mortgage rates are at affordable levels and we would expect affordability to remain strong for the rest of the year," Nothaft added.

On Monday the Commerce Department reported that U.S. August single-family home sales rose 4.7 percent to an annualized rate of 832,000 units. Also, the Conference Board said Tuesday that U.S. leading indicators rose 0.2 percent in August.
The Labor Department will issue September employment data on Friday.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.6 percent on 15-year mortgages, down from 1.7 percent last week, and 1.4 percent on the ARM, unchanged from the previous week.
